title: UK SECR Guide (2026) for Apparel and Footwear
summary: SECR compliance explained for fashion brands: the 6 SECR reporting requirements, deadlines, and real brand examples.
body_markdown:
> Status: ✅ Approved law


If your brand has a large company registered in the UK, it most likely already reports carbon emissions every year. That obligation comes from SECR – Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting.


SECR reporting requirements (Scope 1 and 2 emissions) are light compared to


[frameworks like CSRD](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/csrd-textile) . Yet, on average, SECR


[takes about 94 hours of staff time](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a0dbf75faac4bc0b0e906af/2026-streamlined-energy-and-carbon-reporting-post-implementation-review.pdf) and costs about £7,100 a year. It is also often a brand's first public carbon disclosure, and the baseline everything else builds on.


That baseline matters increasingly in 2026. The UK Sustainability Reporting Standards (UK SRS), which include Scope 3 alongside Scope 1 and 2, become mandatory for listed companies from 2027. The UK is moving towards


[full GHG reporting](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/knowledge/carbon-accounting-guide) .


Let’s break down what SECR compliance means for apparel and footwear companies today, with real examples from brands' own filings!


#### TL;DR


- **What:** SECR requires large UK companies to report their energy use, Scope 1 and 2 emissions, an intensity ratio, and energy efficiency actions in their annual report.


- **Who:** UK quoted companies, plus large UK companies and LLPs that meet 2 of 3 thresholds: £36m+ turnover, £18m+ balance sheet, 250+ employees. This includes the UK subsidiaries of non-UK brands.


- **When:** Every year, in the annual report. The deadline is 9 months after year-end for private companies and 6 months for public companies.


## What Is SECR?


SECR (Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting) is a UK regulation that requires large companies to publish their energy use and carbon emissions every year in their annual report. It has applied to every financial year starting on or after 1 April 2019.
